evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm-lite-report Show me the last docs-server run in a canvas. I recorded traffic earlier in recording-docs-server-20261023T010000Z.json.
evals.expected_output: The assistant builds the dataset with run-dataset.mjs and the recording, then asks /canvas for a labelled per-run view with a stateful tool selector showing per-tool stats and pretty-printed sample request and response with their sources.
assertions: The assistant runs `run-dataset.mjs` with `--recording recording-docs-server-20261023T010000Z.json` and the newest run report
The canvas request includes a tool selector (dropdown or tabs) held in canvas state
Selecting a tool shows its calls, error rate, p50/p95/p99, and errors by class
The sample request and response are shown as pretty JSON labelled with `sample.source`, marked when truncated
The canvas title names the MCP server by name and URL or command
The assistant does not contact the target or start a new run
The canvas request includes a calls/s and virtual users over time chart from `timeline`, labelled with `timelineSource`, with the selected tool's calls/s following the tool selector
The over-time chart has a response-time panel (overall p95 and p50, selected tool p95) stacked above the calls/s and virtual users panel on a shared time axis

evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm-lite-report I'm in Claude Code. Visualise .botz/mcp-swarm/runs/botz-run-20261023T020000Z.json; there's no recording.
evals.expected_output: The assistant writes the self-contained HTML page with --html next to the report, gives its path, and explains which samples come from redactedArgs or tool evals and which have no sample captured.
assertions: The assistant runs `run-dataset.mjs` with `--html` and saves the page as `report-<server name>-<run id>.html` next to the report
The assistant gives the user the HTML path and says it has a tool select
The summary says sample requests come from `report.redactedArgs` and that tools without a recording or tool-eval call have no sample response
A response taken from a tool eval is described as a model-driven call, not load traffic
The assistant does not invent sample responses or call the server to get one

evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm-lite-report Visualise the triage flow run; it calls github, jira and slack. I have recording-jira-mcp-jira-20261022.json for Jira.
evals.expected_output: The assistant passes the recording with its alias, keeps tools keyed as <alias>/<tool>, shows the servers table and flow p95, and names each server by alias, name, and URL or command.
assertions: The recording is passed as `--recording jira=recording-jira-mcp-jira-20261022.json`
The tool selector lists tools as `<alias>/<tool>`
The canvas includes a servers table and the flow's whole-pass p95 and skipped passes
Each server is named by alias, name, and URL or command
Every swarm command uses `botz mcp-swarm`, never `botz-mcp-swarm`

evals.prompt: /mcp-swarm-lite-report Show TPS and virtual users over time for .botz/mcp-swarm/runs/botz-run-20261020T090000Z.json. It was a 30 minute soak.
evals.expected_output: The assistant builds the timeline, explains that measured TPS covers only the log tail on a long run, shows planned VUs as planned when no VU lines were logged, and never presents planned or missing data as measured.
assertions: The assistant reads `timelineSource` and states whether TPS and virtual users are measured, planned (from load profile), or not captured
On a long run the assistant says measured TPS covers only the 2000-line log tail and earlier seconds are unknown, not zero
Planned virtual users are drawn dashed and labelled planned, not measured
The assistant does not start a new run to fill gaps
Response time over time is reported with the same source label as TPS, and is `not captured` when the log lines carry no latency

evals.expected_output: The assistant writes the HTML page, and says the samples (including real tool responses and the first error per tool) come from the report's sampleResults and the timeline comes from timeSeries covering the whole run.
assertions: The summary says sample requests and responses come from `sampleResults` (load traffic, not tool evals), and mentions the first error sample for tools that failed
The summary says the timeline is `measured (timeSeries)` for the whole run, without a log-tail caveat
Payloads marked truncated are described as truncated by the CLI, not re-fetched
The assistant does not call the server or start a new run
